@copilot Update this existing HTTP PR #20881 directly, on its existing head branch. Do not create another PR, change its main base or draft state, or update unrelated branches. The user explicitly approved implementing the following settled 3.0 design through cloud.

getErrorType() returns the final error.type. A null result intentionally omits the attribute, even with an exception or error HTTP status. The extractors must use the getter's result without fallback or their own classification precedence. Retain meaningful default methods on HttpClientAttributesGetter and HttpServerAttributesGetter, but declare getErrorType() abstract on HttpCommonAttributesGetter rather than retaining a role-independent default. Back both role-specific defaults with callable shared classification helpers that instrumentation overrides can also invoke directly. HttpErrorType.forClient/forServer was the illustrative API shape; choose a simple repository-appropriate public API with proper Javadoc, not an inaccessible package-private helper. Do not introduce a generic cross-domain framework.

Replace the interface-qualified super.getErrorType calls in the Reactor Netty and WebFlux cancellation overrides with direct calls to the corresponding helper. Preserve their special cancellation classification and the complete existing HTTP policy: client/server-specific error-status rules, error-status precedence over exceptions, exception-class fallback after non-error statuses, _OTHER for missing/non-positive status without a more specific classification, and omission on successful responses without an exception. Preserve existing handling of positive invalid statuses as well. Reading the HTTP status getter inside a classifier is appropriate only because it explicitly classifies the status by role; do not blindly copy a response status into error.type. Preserve span-status behavior and span/metric consistency. Changing cancellation policy or aligning span status automatically with error.type is outside this PR.

Refresh current main as needed by merging main into this PR head, never the reverse; do not rebase or incorporate unmerged sibling branches. Record the pre-update head and verify it remains on the first-parent chain before pushing. Migrate every affected production override and direct HttpCommonAttributesGetter implementation, and keep focused coverage for authoritative null, custom values, defaults, precedence, and cancellation. Update public API documentation, the API diff, and the concise breaking-change entry as applicable. Follow repository instructions and run narrow formatting and relevant tests. Do not edit the PR title or description; the coordinator handles those after delivery. Do not reply to human comments, resolve unrelated threads, merge PRs, or wait for CI. Stop after the scoped implementation is committed and pushed.
